title: Incident video-review documentation - observed 2024 case
summary: A restricted 2024 incident note documents review of recorded video/audio and a written observation summary. It provides case evidence for an investigation workflow that is independently compatible with the current 2025 surveillance policy, but one case does not establish the complete incident-investigation procedure.

claims.claim: A restricted August 2024 incident record is explicitly a written review of video evidence and records the reviewer's observed sequence of events from the recording.

evidence.page_or_section: restricted 2024 video-review note - structural purpose only
evidence.note: People, allegations and observed case details are excluded.

claims.claim: The current 2025 surveillance policy expressly permits authorized review of recordings for accident investigations, complaints, employee performance review, criminal investigation and other RTEC-determined reasons, corroborating video/audio as a current investigation evidence source.

evidence.page_or_section: printed page 44 - Viewing and Monitoring Policy

claims.claim: Because the 2024 note records an observer's interpretation of a recording rather than the recording itself, investigation records should distinguish source evidence from reviewer observations and final findings.

evidence.note: Process inference; no case conclusion is generalized.

trigger: An incident, complaint or performance issue has relevant RTEC video/audio recording.
prerequisites: Authorized access to the recording under current policy.
actors: Executive Director where access/disclosure decisions apply
steps: Preserve the original recording when investigation/retention rules apply.
Record who reviewed the evidence and when.
Document objective observations separately from interpretations or conclusions.
Corroborate the recording with other available evidence when needed.
Link the review note to the original recording/case and retain access/audit provenance.
decisions: Whether the recording is relevant and requires a retention hold.
Whether additional evidence/witness review is required.
What findings, if any, are supported after complete investigation.
deadlines: Current handbook requires accident-investigation recordings to be retained for three years after the event or until litigation is finally resolved.
outputs: Final finding handled in the governing incident/discipline process
controls: Do not substitute a reviewer summary for preservation of the source recording.
Distinguish observation, interpretation and final finding.
Restrict recording review to authorized roles/current access policy.
Keep case-specific allegations and identities restricted.
unresolved_questions: What current standard form/checklist governs non-accident video investigations?
Is reviewer identity/time/system-access automatically logged today?
How are relevant clips exported, hashed and placed under retention hold when an HR investigation is opened?
automation_candidates: Create an investigation-evidence manifest that hashes recordings/exports and records reviewer, review time, source system and retention hold.
Separate objective timestamped observations from investigator conclusions in the case UI.
Automatically trigger the current surveillance-policy retention workflow when a case references video/audio.

provenance.notes: Names, allegations and case facts excluded.
